newsitem.title: FRANCE: BIS SA,French temp agency, names chairman.
newsitem.headline: BIS SA,French temp agency, names chairman.

text.p: BIS SA a leading French temporary help agency, has appointed board member Claude Charbonniaud as chairman to succeed the firm's founder Laurent Negro who died last weekend.
"He will direct the group continuing the policies defined by Mr. Laurent Negro at the general assembly on June 19, 1996," Bis said in a statement issued following a special board meeting on Tuesday.
Analysts said earlier this week that Negro's death could accelerate Bis's quest to link up with another temporary help firm.
The U.S. temporary help firm Manpower had been suggested as a possible partner, but French newspaper Liberation reported on Wednesday that Manpower France had ruled out the idea.

Bis has been accused by some critics of being too focused on France. At the June shareholders' meeting, Negro , who pioneered temporary help services in France, said that Bis needed to "wake up" and take part in the wave of consolidation sweeping the sector. He praised the merger last May between French manpower agency Ecco SA and Swiss personnel company Adia.
Negro had said that BIS was searching for an international alliance "to satisfy multinational clients who reproach us for not being in New York or Tokyo" but did not identify any potential partners.
Negro and his family held over 50 percent of BIS, which has 4,800 employees and a network of 500 agencies.
Bis added that its unit, Caisse Fonciere de Credit, had sold nearly all of its loan portfolio to "a pool of Anglo-Saxon investors, allowing it to put a clear end to its losses."
The 270 million francs raised from the disposal will be used to reimburse Caisse Fonciere's debts to Bis SA, Bis said.
It said Caisse Fonciere de Credit's operations would appear in Bis SA's accounts as a non-recurring loss estimated at 215 million francs.

Bis posted a first-half profit of 34 million francs, down from 70 million a year earlier. It forecast that 1996 full-year results would be sharply below the previous year's profit of 201 million francs, due partly to poor trading conditions.
